name: Imperial Jade
lede: Imperial Jade is a strong, slightly blue-leaning green named for the most prized grade of jade, the gem that gives its name to one whole green family in our library.

sections.title: The top grade of the gem
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates this name to 1927, at plate 21, L 12 [1]. "Imperial" marks it as the finest grade of [[gem:jade|jade]], the vivid, slightly translucent green jadeite associated with Chinese carving and ornament, rather than the duller, more common nephrite [1]. This entry has no Ridgway plate of its own, so the 1927 date is the earliest recorded here [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[imperial-jade]], [[sea-green]] and [[emeraude]], at 3.2, 4.6 and 4.6 ΔE [1]. It reads itself than to the brighter, bluer [[emerald]], consistent with its gemstone name [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this green in only 20 of 23,781 paintings, under one tenth of one per cent [2]. It peaks hard in the 1900s, at nearly eight times the overall baseline rate, consistent with a name only recorded from 1927 [2]. The earliest match is an 1835 portrait by Francis Alexander, almost a century before the name was recorded, so that is a lookalike hue and not evidence the color was named that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and a match is not a test for jadeite or any other mineral [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
